chapter: Chicago, Villa Venice and Louis Armstrong
title: First Chicago band: Ed Cary, Guy Kelly and the Cary family
summary: Budd recalls his first Chicago band under Ed Cary and its members while Hinton adds that Scoops Cary was his classmate.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: So some of the first people I met -- well the first band I played with in Chicago was Ed Cary, and Guy Kelly, and --
-- (Jerry Sidney) Bonham, and what was the piano player's name? Oh -- gee, he was a little sweet, too, wasn't he?
No, Kenneth was a great, great --
No, Sammy, no, no. But anyway --
No, not Jerome. Jerome was a beautiful man.
I'm telling you, this is what led me on the piano. Anyway, I was playing -- Ed Cary was a great arranger, you know that?
He could write. And then his brother Scoops Cary was in the band.
Scoops and I graduated from high school together.
Ed Wood Cary's father, father Cary, father was a --
Was a real estate man, wasn't he.
-- real estate man, and insurance man.
And his mother was very talented, too.
And they were from Arkansas, right?
And they migrated to Chicago, and Zelly Bonham. I met all of these great, great trumpet players, man.
